text.p: The new school year marks the beginning of the sports season, including the popular game of football.
Experts say more than 2.5 million players will be taking to the football field this season, and over 200,000 of them will have a serious head injury.
Many others will have concussions of varying degrees of severity.

A form-fitting helmet shell, the ProCap, is being studied by the Pennsylvania State University Biomechanics Laboratory and George Washington University Hospital Sports Medicine Department to determine whether it helps reduce the number of serious head and neck injuries received playing football.
Protective Sports Inc., of Erie, Pa., said the studies show that its product, which is worn on top of conventional hard-shell helmets, can greatly reduce the risk of serious head and neck injuries.
ProCap designer Bert Strauss said from Erie that the ProCap is made of a soft foam-like material, and has an outer cover "that's slippery to the touch."
The device is worn over the regulation football helmet and is held in place by Velcro straps.

Strayss said the National Football League has asked that more information be made available to determine what, if any, effect the protective gear's softer surface had on deflecting head-on impact blows, compared with conventional hard-shell helmets.

The Penn State study showed that ProCap's soft shell deflected head-on impact blows equally as well as the hard-shell helmets. However, its study showed that head-on impact resulted in less critical force on the vertebral column in those players wearing helmets covered with the ProCap than those without.

The George Washington study involved student athletes from several Washington, D.C.-area public and private high schools. Players randomly selected to wear the ProCap had fewer concussions and neck strains than those players who wore conventional helmets alone.
Strauss said that the ProCap was first used by a professional football player in 1989 but is now available for children, teens and adult players.
The ProCap costs $55. When selecting the right size, note the player's helmet make, size and colour.
For more information, call 1-800-444-1146.
A new guide for fix-it-yourselfers says some of the most complicated problems have some of the simplest solutions.
Dropped your camera in the swimming pool and fear you have to throw it out? First, remove the batteries and if you can't have it serviced immediately, freeze it to limit potential damage.
Try running an ordinary magnet along your screwdriver to make starting small screws easier.
Before scrapping a malfunctioning VCR, unplug and replug all the wires, scraping off any corrosion that may be causing poor contact. This could be just the ticket to save you money on a new machine.

These words of wisdom are included in the "New Fix-It-Yourself Manual: How to Repair, Clean and Maintain Anything and Everything In and Around Your Home," published this month by the Readers Digest Association.
It costs $35 hardcover.

The book contains a detailed introduction to tools and their uses; tips to simplify repair; guidelines for buying equipment and appliances; information on plumbing repairs; and what to do in the case of home emergencies.
For more information on the book, call 1-800-788-6262.
The Healthy Choice line of prepared foods, produced by ConAgra Inc., is introducing eight new frozen meals, its largest product introduction since the line debuted in 1988.

All of the varieties meet the U.S. Government's definition of "healthy," containing lower levels of fat, 90 milligrams or less of cholesterol, less than 600 milligrams of sodium and at least 10 percent of the daily value of nutrients including vitamin A, vitamin C, calcium, iron, protein or fiber.

The new meals include: roasted chicken, herb baked fish, grilled glazed pork patty, grilled chicken Sonoma, grilled peppercorn steak patty, penne pasta with roasted tomato sauce, grilled chicken with mashed potatoes, and vegetable french bread pizza.
Suggested retail prices for these new meals and entrees range from $1.99 to $2.99. They should be available nation-wide this month.
